newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude trading slows, Murban premium slides.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude trading slows, Murban premium slides.

text.p: Asian crude trading set a slower pace on Tuesday with most of the latest trading month done, amid lower talk on Murban premiums.
Traders said a European major sold a Murban cargo to a U.S. major at ADNOC +10 to +12 cents, down from recent deals which have mostly been around +17.
They said the fall in premium had been expected as a few sellers emerged in recent days, but were faced with few buyers.
Oman held steady, with a European major heard selling 400,000 barrels of the grade to China at MPM +9 cents, in line with recent deals.
Market sources said most of MidEast March barrels were now placed. They said some Oman was left and a European major still had Murban to sell.
Dubai was almost entirely placed, but the Indian tender, which closes on Thursday, might tempt some holders to offer the grade into the tender.
The IOC traditionally takes Dubai crude oil in its monthly tenders.
Intermonth Dubai spreads rose on the tight supply late last week, but have held steady since in the run up to the Indian tender.
On Tuesday, March/April was talked at 40/45 cents and April/May at 37/43. Brent/Dubai was steady also, with most actively talked April around $1.90/$2.00.
Regional grades were also mostly done for February.
Indonesia's benchmark Minas grade was already being offered for March as low as ICP +65/70 cents, down from February when most deals were done above ICP +$1.00.
Traders said weak margins and refineries' move into spring schedules would limit demand for regional grades in March.
